question: What time do Quillfen studios close on Fridays?
answer: Quillfen studios close at 1 p.m. on Fridays.

sources.title: Quillfen Staff Handbook - Annual leave
sources.text:
Everyone at Quillfen Architects receives 27 days of paid annual leave a year, plus public holidays, rising to 30 days after five years with the practice. The leave year runs from 1 April to 31 March.

Booking leave
Request leave in the HR system and copy in your project lead. Try to give at least four weeks' notice for anything longer than a week, and check the project calendar first so that you are not away during a planned submission or a key client presentation.

Sickness during leave
If you are ill during a period of annual leave, tell your line manager as soon as you can. Days of illness covered by a fit note can be reclaimed and taken as annual leave at another time.

Carrying over leave
Up to five days can be carried over into the next leave year with your project lead's agreement. Carried-over days must be used by 30 June.

Buying extra leave
Once a year, in March, you can buy up to five extra days of leave. The cost is spread across your salary payments for the following twelve months.

sources.title: Quillfen Staff Handbook - Professional registration and CPD
sources.text:
Quillfen supports architects, architectural assistants and technologists in gaining and keeping their professional registration.

Registration fees
The practice pays the annual registration fee and one professional institute membership for every member of staff who holds, or is working towards, a professional qualification. Submit the invoice to the finance team before the renewal date and they will pay it directly.

Continuing professional development
Registered architects must complete at least 35 hours of CPD each year. Quillfen runs a lunchtime CPD talk every other Wednesday, covering topics such as building regulations, fire safety, sustainable materials and contract law. Talks are recorded and saved to the learning library for anyone who cannot attend.

Study leave for qualifications
If you are studying for Part 2 or Part 3, you can take up to ten days of paid study leave a year for exams and submissions, in addition to annual leave. Agree the dates with your project lead as early as you can.

Keeping records
Log your CPD hours in the HR system. Your line manager reviews them with you at your mid-year conversation.

sources.title: Quillfen Staff Handbook - Summer Fridays
sources.text:
Summer Fridays give everyone at Quillfen time to enjoy the long evenings while the weather is good.

Between 4 June and 27 August 2027, Quillfen studios close at 1 p.m. on Fridays. The closed afternoons are paid and do not count against your annual leave.

Client commitments
Project deadlines, site visits and client meetings still come first. If a planning hearing, site inspection or client presentation is booked for a Friday afternoon during this period, your project lead will agree with you who needs to attend. Anyone who works a Friday afternoon during the period can take the same number of hours off on another day within four weeks, agreed with their project lead.

Part-time staff
If you do not normally work on Fridays, you can take an equivalent half day on another day in the same week, agreed with your project lead.

Getting into the building
The studio buildings are locked from 1.30 p.m. on these Fridays, and the alarm is set at 2 p.m. If you need to collect drawings or models after that time, ask the office manager in advance for an out-of-hours pass. Remote access to the project server and email is available as usual.

gold.target_claim: Quillfen Architects' studios close at 1 p.m. on Fridays all year round.

gold_spans.quote: Between 4 June and 27 August 2027, Quillfen studios close at 1 p.m. on Fridays.

construction.note: Deleted only the date range (and its comma); S3 sets the 1 p.m. Friday closing for 4 June to 27 August 2027 only and states no hours for other Fridays, so a year-round 1 p.m. closing is unsupported.

question: Can I bring my dog or cat in the cabin on Merrowind Air?
answer: Small dogs and cats can travel in the cabin in a soft-sided carrier that fits under the seat in front of you.

sources.title: Merrowind Air - Pets in the cabin
sources.text:
On domestic flights, small dogs and cats can travel in the cabin in a soft-sided carrier that fits under the seat in front of you. The carrier can be no larger than 45 x 30 x 25 cm, and your pet must stay inside it, with the carrier closed, for the whole flight, including take-off, landing and taxiing.

Adding your pet to a booking
Call our reservations team at least 48 hours before departure to add your pet to your booking. Pets cannot be added in the app or at the airport. The pet fee is $95 for each flight and is paid when your pet is added.

Each passenger can bring one pet carrier. The carrier counts as your personal item, but you can still bring one cabin bag for the overhead locker.

Before you fly
Your pet must be at least 10 weeks old and able to stand up and turn around inside the carrier. Make sure your pet has had a chance to eat, drink and go to the toilet before you leave for the airport. Please check in at the airport desk rather than online, so that our staff can check the carrier and attach a pet tag to it.

On board
You will be seated in a window seat, away from the exit rows. Your pet must not be taken out of the carrier during the flight and must not be given food on board, although small amounts of water are fine.

sources.title: Merrowind Air - Flying with infants
sources.text:
Children under two years old can travel on your lap rather than in their own seat. Each adult can hold one infant on their lap, and the infant must be added to the booking when you book or later in Manage Booking. Infants on your lap travel for 10% of the adult fare, plus taxes.

Infant seats
If you would like your child to have their own seat, you can book a child ticket for them and bring an approved car seat. The car seat must fit in a standard economy seat and carry a label showing it is approved for use in aircraft.

Bassinets
A limited number of bassinets are available on flights longer than four hours, for babies weighing up to 10 kg. Request one by calling our reservations team. Bassinets are given out in the order requests are received.

Strollers and car seats
You can check in one stroller and one car seat for each child at no charge, in addition to your normal baggage allowance. Folding strollers can be left at the aircraft door and returned to you when you get off.

Feeding
You are welcome to bring baby food, formula and milk through security in reasonable quantities for your journey.

sources.title: Merrowind Air - Check-in times
sources.text:
Online check-in for Merrowind Air flights opens 24 hours before departure. You can check in on our website or in the app and keep your boarding pass on your phone.

When check-in closes
For domestic flights, check-in closes 45 minutes before departure. For international flights, check-in closes 60 minutes before departure. These times apply whether you check in online or at the airport desk, and they also apply to bag drop.

Who needs to check in at the desk
You will need to check in at an airport desk if you are travelling with an infant on your lap who is not yet on your booking, or with sporting equipment that must be measured. Desks open three hours before departure.

At the gate
Boarding starts 40 minutes before departure. The gate closes 15 minutes before departure, and we cannot hold the flight for passengers who arrive after this.

Documents
For international flights, bring a passport that is valid for the whole of your trip. We may also need to see your visa or residence permit at check-in.

gold.target_claim: Small dogs and cats can travel in the cabin in a soft-sided under-seat carrier on any Merrowind Air flight, not only domestic ones.

gold_spans.quote: On domestic flights, small dogs and cats can travel in the cabin in a soft-sided carrier that fits under the seat in front of you.

construction.note: Deleted only the 'On domestic flights' scope (and capitalised 'Small'); S1 allows cabin pets on domestic flights and no passage says anything about pets on international flights, so the unscoped claim is unsupported.

question: Can I get back a photo I deleted in Ferrowyn Photos?
answer: You can restore deleted photos from the Recently Deleted album.

sources.title: Ferrowyn Photos - Storage plans
sources.text:
Every Ferrowyn account comes with 15 GB of free storage for your photos and videos. Photos and videos are stored at their original quality, and the space they use is shown in the app under Account > Storage.

Paid plans
If you need more space, you can upgrade to a paid plan from Account > Storage:
- Plus: 200 GB for $2.99 per month
- Family: 2 TB for $9.99 per month, shared with up to five other people

Plans renew automatically each month until you cancel. If you cancel, your plan stays active until the end of the month you have paid for.

Sharing a Family plan
The person who buys the Family plan can invite up to five people from Account > Family. Each member's photos stay private unless they choose to share them, and the app shows how much space each person is using.

If you run out of space
When your storage is full, new photos and videos stop uploading from your devices until you free up space or upgrade. Photos that are already in your library are not affected.

sources.title: Ferrowyn Photos - Face grouping and your privacy
sources.text:
Face grouping helps you find photos of the people who matter to you. When it is turned on, Ferrowyn Photos looks for faces in your library and puts photos of the same person together under People, so you can name them and search by name.

How face grouping works
To group faces, Ferrowyn creates a face model for each person it finds: a set of numbers that describes the shape of a face. Face models are used only for grouping photos in your own library. They are not used to identify people in other users' libraries, and they are never shared with advertisers.

Turning face grouping off
You can turn face grouping on or off at any time under Settings > Privacy > Face grouping. When you turn it off, the People section disappears and the face models created from your library are deleted within 14 days. Your photos themselves are not deleted.

Names you add
Names you give to people in your library are visible only to you. If you share an album, the people in it are not labelled for the people you share it with.

sources.title: Ferrowyn Photos - Deleting photos and videos
sources.text:
When you delete a photo or video in Ferrowyn Photos, it is removed from your library on every phone, tablet and computer signed in to your Ferrowyn account. If the photo was in a shared album, it is removed from that album too, and the people you shared it with will no longer see it.

Getting a photo back
You can restore deleted photos from the Recently Deleted album during the first 30 days after you delete them. To restore a photo, open Albums > Recently Deleted, select the photo and tap Restore. It goes back to its original place in your library, with its date, location and album information unchanged.

Recently Deleted and your storage
Photos and videos in Recently Deleted do not count toward your storage quota. Only you can see your Recently Deleted album, and it is not included when you share your library with a partner or family member.

Copies stored elsewhere
Deleting a photo in Ferrowyn Photos does not delete copies you have saved somewhere else, such as on a memory card, in a computer folder that is not synced with Ferrowyn, or in a messaging app.

Deleting many photos at once
To delete several photos, tap Select, choose the photos and tap the bin icon. You can also select a whole day or month at once by tapping its date heading.

gold.target_claim: Ferrowyn Photos users can restore deleted photos from the Recently Deleted album with no time limit.

gold_spans.quote: You can restore deleted photos from the Recently Deleted album during the first 30 days after you delete them.

gold.dropped_qualifier: during the first 30 days after you delete them

construction.note: Deleted only the 30-day period; S3 supports restoring during the first 30 days after deletion and no passage says what happens after that, so the claim of restoration with no time limit is unsupported.

question: What should I expect when I call the v2 endpoints of the Corvinth Storage API?
answer: Every response to a request sent to the v2 endpoints of the Corvinth Storage API includes a Deprecation header.

sources.title: Corvinth Storage SDK - Configuring credentials
sources.text:
The Corvinth Storage SDK looks for credentials in a fixed order and uses the first set it finds. First, it checks for credentials passed directly to the client when it is created. Next, it reads the CORVINTH_ACCESS_KEY and CORVINTH_SECRET_KEY environment variables. Finally, it reads the default profile from the credentials file in your home directory.

For applications running on Corvinth Compute, you do not need to store keys at all. Attach a service identity to the instance, and the SDK fetches short-lived credentials from the instance metadata service and refreshes them before they expire.

Avoid putting access keys in source code. If keys are committed to a repository by mistake, revoke them in the console straight away and create new ones; revoked keys stop working within a minute.

You can confirm which credentials the SDK picked up by turning on debug logging. The log shows the source that was used, such as environment or profile, but never prints the secret key itself.

sources.title: Corvinth Storage - Buckets and object naming
sources.text:
Objects in Corvinth Storage are kept in buckets. A bucket name must be between 3 and 63 characters long, use only lowercase letters, numbers and hyphens, and be unique within your Corvinth organisation. Bucket names cannot be changed after creation, so choose one that will still make sense later.

Object keys can be up to 1,024 bytes long when encoded as UTF-8. Slashes in a key are treated as ordinary characters, but the console and the SDKs display them as folders, which makes it easy to organise objects by date, customer or type. There is no limit on the number of objects in a bucket.

Each bucket belongs to one storage region, chosen when the bucket is created. Objects never leave that region unless you copy them to a bucket elsewhere. Moving a bucket to another region is not possible; instead, create a new bucket in the target region and copy the objects across with the transfer tool.

Versioning can be turned on per bucket. When it is on, overwriting or deleting an object keeps the previous copy as a noncurrent version, which you can restore or remove later.

sources.title: Corvinth Storage API - Moving from v2 to v3
sources.text:
Version 3 of the Corvinth Storage API became generally available on 14 September 2026. It adds resumable uploads for objects over 5 GB, conditional writes, and a consistent error format across all endpoints. New integrations should be built on v3.

Between 1 March and 31 August 2027, every response to a request sent to the v2 endpoints of the Corvinth Storage API includes a Deprecation header. A Link header in the same response points to the v2 to v3 migration guide. Most HTTP client libraries ignore these headers unless you read them, so we recommend logging them in your application to find code that still calls v2.

Most integrations need only small changes to move to v3. The base path changes from /v2 to /v3, object listings are paginated with a continuation token instead of a page number, and error responses use a single JSON shape with a code, a message and a request ID. The migration guide lists every change with before-and-after examples.

You can call v2 and v3 from the same application with the same access keys, so services can be moved one at a time. The Usage page in the Corvinth console shows request counts split by API version, which helps you confirm when the last v2 call has gone.

gold.target_claim: Every response to a request sent to the Corvinth Storage API's v2 endpoints includes a Deprecation header.

gold_spans.quote: Between 1 March and 31 August 2027, every response to a request sent to the v2 endpoints of the Corvinth Storage API includes a Deprecation header.

construction.note: Deleted only the window 'Between 1 March and 31 August 2027' and recapitalised the sentence; S3 states the header for that window only and no passage says what v2 responses carry before or after it, so the undated claim is unsupported.

question: Is there a discount on Ostrevia CRM annual subscriptions?
answer: Ostrevia CRM discounts the first year of any new annual subscription by 25%.

sources.title: Ostrevia CRM - Annual subscription offer
sources.text:
Between 1 February and 31 March 2027, Ostrevia CRM discounts the first year of any new annual subscription by 25%. The discount applies to every edition of Ostrevia CRM (Essentials, Professional and Enterprise) and to any number of seats bought when the subscription starts.

The discount is applied automatically at checkout, so there is no code to enter. Your order summary shows the list price, the discount and the amount you will pay before you confirm. Customers who buy through an Ostrevia partner see the discount on the partner's quote instead.

Seats added later in the first year are charged at the same discounted per-seat rate as the seats bought at the start, prorated to the end of the annual term.

A new subscription means one created for an organisation that has not had a paid Ostrevia CRM subscription in the last 12 months. Organisations that are still on a free trial count as new, and a trial can be converted to an annual plan from the Billing page at any time during the trial.

If you are not sure whether your organisation qualifies, contact our sales team from the Pricing page.

sources.title: Ostrevia CRM - Importing contacts from a spreadsheet
sources.text:
You can bring contacts into Ostrevia CRM from a CSV or Excel file. Go to Contacts, choose Import, and upload your file. Files can have up to 50,000 rows and 200 columns.

After the upload, Ostrevia shows each column from your file next to a suggested CRM field. Check the suggestions and change any that are wrong; columns you do not need can be skipped. If a column does not match any existing field, you can create a new custom field from the same screen.

Duplicates are matched on email address. For each duplicate you can choose to skip the row, update the existing contact with any values that are empty, or overwrite the existing values. The default is to update empty values only, which avoids replacing information your team has entered by hand.

Imports run in the background, and you will receive an email with a summary when they finish, including a downloadable file of any rows that could not be imported and the reason for each one.

sources.title: Ostrevia CRM - Editions compared
sources.text:
Ostrevia CRM comes in three editions. Essentials covers contact and company records, a shared inbox, and a single sales pipeline with up to 10 custom stages. Professional adds multiple pipelines, sales sequences, quotes with e-signature, and custom reports. Enterprise adds field-level permissions, sandbox environments for testing changes, and a 99.9% uptime commitment backed by service credits.

Every edition includes the Ostrevia mobile app for iOS and Android, two-way calendar sync, and import tools for moving records from spreadsheets and other CRMs. Data is stored in the region you choose when you sign up and can be exported at any time as CSV files.

You can mix editions within one organisation only on Enterprise, where some teams can be given Professional seats. On Essentials and Professional, every seat in the organisation is on the same edition.

To compare editions side by side, including limits on custom fields, automation rules and API calls, open the comparison table on the Pricing page.

gold.target_claim: Ostrevia CRM discounts the first year of any new annual subscription by 25%.

gold_spans.quote: Between 1 February and 31 March 2027, Ostrevia CRM discounts the first year of any new annual subscription by 25%.

construction.note: Deleted only the window 'Between 1 February and 31 March 2027' and recapitalised the sentence; S1 states the 25% discount for that window only and no passage says what applies at other times, so the undated discount is unsupported.

question: I bought Tessaline Cloud through Arbourline Marketplace; how long do I have to cancel an annual plan and get a refund?
answer: Arbourline Marketplace refunds an annual Tessaline Cloud plan if it is cancelled within 30 days of purchase.

sources.title: Buying Tessaline Cloud through Arbourline Marketplace
sources.text:
Tessaline Cloud plans can also be bought through Arbourline Marketplace, a software marketplace that lets companies pay for several vendors on one invoice. Plans bought this way are billed by Arbourline Marketplace, not by Tessaline Cloud, and refunds follow Arbourline Marketplace's terms rather than Tessaline Cloud's own refund policy.

Arbourline Marketplace refunds an annual Tessaline Cloud plan only if the cancellation is made within 14 days of purchase. Refund requests must be submitted through the Arbourline Marketplace order page, and Tessaline Cloud support cannot issue or approve them.

Features, limits and outbound transfer allowances are the same whether a plan is bought directly or through the marketplace. Marketplace prices may differ slightly from list prices because Arbourline Marketplace converts them into the buyer's invoice currency at the start of each term.

sources.title: Refunds for annual subscriptions
sources.text:
Tessaline Cloud charges annual subscriptions up front for the full twelve-month term. Tessaline Cloud refunds the full amount paid for an annual plan that is cancelled within 30 days of the original purchase date, provided the workspace has used less than 50 GB of outbound data transfer during that period. After the 30-day window, annual plans are not refundable, but the workspace keeps access to all paid features until the end of the term that has already been paid for.

Refunds go back to the original payment method. Card refunds typically appear on the cardholder's statement within 5 to 10 business days. Refunds for invoices paid by bank transfer are issued as a credit note first and then paid out within 15 business days. Taxes that were remitted to a tax authority on the customer's behalf are not refunded unless the authority returns them to Tessaline Cloud.

Only the workspace owner can request a refund, using Settings > Billing > Request a refund. Requests sent by other workspace members, or emailed to a support agent, cannot be processed.

gold.target_claim: Arbourline Marketplace refunds an annual Tessaline Cloud plan cancelled within 30 days of purchase.

gold_spans.quote: Arbourline Marketplace refunds an annual Tessaline Cloud plan only if the cancellation is made within 14 days of purchase.
Tessaline Cloud refunds the full amount paid for an annual plan that is cancelled within 30 days of the original purchase date

construction.note: The 30-day window is Tessaline Cloud's own direct-purchase policy (S2); the answer attributes it to Arbourline Marketplace, which S1 says refunds only within 14 days. Reuses the s1-f1 refund passage.

question: Does Saltmere Helpdesk offer a discount for Canadian charities?
answer: Registered charities in Canada receive 40% off Saltmere Helpdesk's Growth plan.

sources.title: Saltmere Helpdesk plans
sources.text:
Saltmere Helpdesk has two paid plans. The Essentials plan costs $15 per agent per month and covers email and web-form tickets, a shared inbox, canned replies and basic reporting. The Growth plan costs $39 per agent per month and adds live chat, a public help centre, service-level targets, custom ticket fields and scheduled reports.

Both plans are available on monthly or annual billing. Annual billing costs the same as eleven months of monthly billing. Agent seats can be added at any time and are prorated for the rest of the billing period.

Light agents, who can view tickets and add internal notes but cannot reply to customers, are free on the Growth plan and limited to 5 per workspace on Essentials. Every workspace can start with a 14-day free trial of the Growth plan, and trial workspaces are not charged until a plan is chosen.

sources.title: Nonprofit discount
sources.text:
Saltmere Helpdesk offers a discount to eligible nonprofit organisations. Registered charities in the United Kingdom and Ireland receive 40% off the Growth plan, on either monthly or annual billing. The discount applies to every agent seat in the workspace and continues for as long as the organisation remains registered.

To apply, the workspace owner submits the organisation's charity registration number from Settings > Billing > Nonprofit programme. Applications are usually reviewed within 5 business days. If an application is approved, the discount starts on the next invoice; earlier invoices are not adjusted.

Saltmere Helpdesk checks registration status once a year. If a registration lapses, the workspace is notified and the discount ends at the following renewal. The nonprofit discount cannot be combined with other promotional offers, and it does not apply to add-ons such as the Voice channel or the AI reply assistant.

gold.target_claim: Registered charities in Canada receive 40% off Saltmere Helpdesk's Growth plan.

gold_spans.quote: Registered charities in the United Kingdom and Ireland receive 40% off the Growth plan

construction.note: S2 gives the 40% discount to registered charities in the United Kingdom and Ireland; Canada is neither covered nor explicitly excluded, so the claim is unsupported rather than contradicted.

question: Do Studio sub-accounts under our Tarrowfield Scheduling Growth plan get the Payments add-on for free?
answer: Studio sub-accounts created by a Growth plan organisation get the Payments add-on at no extra charge.

sources.title: Studio sub-accounts
sources.text:
Organisations that run several locations can create Studio sub-accounts, so that each location has its own booking page, staff calendars, opening hours and branding. Organisations on the Growth plan can create Studio sub-accounts from Settings > Organisation > Studios, and there is no limit on the number of Studios per organisation.

Each Studio sub-account is billed on the parent organisation's monthly invoice, with its calendars listed as a separate line so that costs can be split between locations. Studio managers can edit their own Studio's services, staff and opening hours but cannot see other Studios' bookings or the organisation's invoices. Add-ons are switched on separately for each Studio from that Studio's own settings page.

Studios can be renamed at any time without changing their booking page address. Deleting a Studio cancels its future bookings and sends the affected clients an email explaining that the appointment has been cancelled.

sources.title: Tarrowfield Scheduling plans
sources.text:
Tarrowfield Scheduling has three plans for appointment-based businesses. The Solo plan costs $12 per month for one staff calendar and includes online booking, email reminders and a booking page with your logo. On the Solo plan, the Payments add-on can be bought for $15 per month.

The Growth plan costs $9 per staff calendar per month, with a minimum of 3 calendars. It adds text message reminders, group classes and intake forms. The Growth plan includes the Payments add-on at no extra charge for every staff calendar in the workspace, so clients can pay deposits or full fees when they book.

The Enterprise plan is priced by quote and adds single sign-on, custom data retention and an uptime commitment. Card processing fees charged by the payment provider apply on every plan and are not set by Tarrowfield Scheduling.

gold.target_claim: Studio sub-accounts created by a Growth plan organisation get the Payments add-on at no extra charge.

gold_spans.quote: Organisations on the Growth plan can create Studio sub-accounts
The Growth plan includes the Payments add-on at no extra charge for every staff calendar in the workspace

construction.note: Needs the unstated bridge that a Studio's calendars count as staff calendars in the parent Growth workspace (or that Studios inherit Growth pricing for add-ons); S1 says Studios are billed on the parent invoice and switch add-ons on separately, but never whether Payments is free for them, so the passages do not jointly entail the claim.

question: What will the Orvane Analytics Team plan cost after the price change?
answer: From 1 March 2026, the Team plan costs $22 per seat per month.

sources.title: Team plan price change
sources.text:
Orvane Analytics is changing the price of the Team plan for the first time since the plan launched. From 1 March 2026, the Team plan costs $22 per seat per month for workspaces with a billing address in the United States or Canada. Until that date, those workspaces continue to pay the current price of $18 per seat per month. Workspaces with a billing address in any other country are on regional pricing, which is being reviewed separately and is not covered by this notice.

The new price applies to every seat in the workspace, including seats that were added before the change. Features and event allowances on the Team plan are not changing as part of this update. Orvane Analytics emails the owners of affected workspaces at least 45 days before the new price takes effect, and the notice also appears as a banner on the Billing page.

Owners who decide not to continue can cancel from the Billing page before their next renewal date. Cancelling does not delete project data, which stays readable for 30 days after the subscription ends.

sources.title: Event allowances by plan
sources.text:
Every Orvane Analytics plan includes a monthly allowance of tracked events. The Free plan includes 50,000 events per month across up to three seats. The Team plan includes 2 million events per month, shared across all seats in the workspace. The Business plan includes 10 million events per month and adds data warehouse export.

The allowance resets on the first day of each calendar month, regardless of when the workspace was created. Unused events do not carry over. When a workspace reaches 80% of its allowance, owners and admins receive an email, and a second email is sent at 100%.

Events sent after the allowance is used up are still collected, but they are held in a queue and cannot be queried until the workspace upgrades or the next month begins. Queued events are kept for 14 days; anything older is discarded. Raw event data on all paid plans is retained for 25 months.

sources.title: Adding and removing seats
sources.text:
Owners and admins can add seats to an Orvane Analytics workspace at any time from Settings > Members. A seat is needed for every person who can sign in, including read-only viewers on the Team plan. Seats added partway through a billing period are charged immediately for the days left in that period, and the full seat price is included on the next invoice.

Removing a seat does not trigger a refund for the current period. Instead, the removed seat stops being billed from the next invoice onward. If a workspace removes seats and adds them back within the same billing period, the re-added seats are not charged twice.

Workspaces on the Business plan can buy seats in packs of ten at a lower per-seat rate. Pack pricing is agreed with the sales team and is shown on the order form rather than on the public pricing page. Guests invited to a single shared dashboard do not need a seat.

gold.target_claim: From 1 March 2026, the Orvane Analytics Team plan costs $22 per seat per month for all workspaces.

gold_spans.quote: From 1 March 2026, the Team plan costs $22 per seat per month for workspaces with a billing address in the United States or Canada.

gold.dropped_qualifier: for workspaces with a billing address in the United States or Canada

construction.note: The United States/Canada billing-address scope was deleted; S1 says pricing elsewhere is regional and not covered, so the universal price claim is not supported.

question: What do workspaces get under the Pallister Docs autumn upgrade offer?
answer: Workspaces that upgrade to the annual Business plan receive 3 additional months free.

sources.title: Switching between monthly and annual billing
sources.text:
Workspace owners can change the billing interval from Settings > Billing at any time. When a workspace moves from monthly to annual billing, Pallister Docs credits the unused part of the current month and applies that credit to the first annual invoice. The annual term starts on the day of the switch.

Moving from annual to monthly billing takes effect at the end of the current annual term. Until then, the workspace stays on annual billing and keeps its annual price. Pallister Docs sends a reminder email 30 days before an annual term renews, showing the editor count and price that will be charged.

The billing interval applies to the whole workspace; individual editors cannot be billed on a different interval. Invoices are issued in US dollars, euros or pounds sterling depending on the billing country, and the currency cannot be changed once the first invoice has been paid.

sources.title: Pallister Docs plans
sources.text:
Pallister Docs has three plans. The Free plan is for individuals and small groups: up to 3 editors, unlimited viewers, 1 GB of file storage per workspace and 30 days of page history.

The Plus plan costs $10 per editor per month on monthly billing or $96 per editor per year on annual billing. It includes unlimited editors, 100 GB of storage, 1 year of page history and guest access for up to 20 external collaborators.

The Business plan costs $20 per editor per month on monthly billing or $192 per editor per year on annual billing. It adds single sign-on, audit logs, unlimited page history, 1 TB of storage and admin controls for sharing outside the organisation.

Viewers, who can read and comment but not edit, are free on every plan. A workspace is billed for the highest number of editors it had at any point during the billing period.

sources.title: Autumn upgrade offer
sources.text:
From 1 October to 30 November 2026, Pallister Docs is adding free months to new annual subscriptions. The free months are added to the end of the workspace's first annual term, so the first renewal date moves later while the first annual charge stays the same.

Workspaces that upgrade to the annual Business plan between 1 October and 30 November 2026 receive 3 additional months free. Workspaces that upgrade to the annual Plus plan in the same period receive 1 additional month free. Monthly subscriptions started during the offer period do not qualify, and switching an existing annual subscription to a different annual plan does not count as an upgrade.

Free months earned under the offer stay with the workspace that earned them. They cannot be moved to another workspace, exchanged for a discount on a later renewal, or paid out as credit if the subscription is cancelled. If a workspace downgrades from Business to Plus during its first annual term, any free months it has not yet used are reduced from 3 to 1.

question: Can a cancelled Kestrowe CRM account be reactivated?
answer: A cancelled Kestrowe CRM account can be reactivated with all of its data within 90 days of cancellation.

sources.title: Moving to the Free plan instead of cancelling
sources.text:
Instead of cancelling, a Kestrowe CRM account can move to the Free plan from Billing > Subscription > Change plan. The Free plan allows 2 users, 1,000 contacts and one sales pipeline. Workflow automations, email sequences and the reporting dashboard are not available on Free.

The move to Free happens at the end of the current billing period. If the account has more users than the Free plan allows, the owner chooses which 2 users stay active; the others are deactivated but keep their history, so their deals and notes still appear in the account. Contacts above the 1,000 limit are not deleted. They stay visible and searchable but cannot be edited until the account upgrades again or the total drops below the limit.

Extra pipelines become read-only. Automations are paused rather than deleted, and they resume with their previous settings if the account returns to a paid plan.

sources.title: Cancelling your Kestrowe CRM subscription
sources.text:
An account owner can cancel a Kestrowe CRM subscription at any time from Billing > Subscription > Cancel plan. Cancellation stops future renewals. The account keeps its paid features until the end of the current billing period and then moves to a read-only archived state.

If the account owner did not request immediate deletion, a cancelled Kestrowe CRM account can be reactivated with all of its data within 90 days of cancellation. Reactivation is done from the same Billing page and restores contacts, deals, pipelines, notes and attachments exactly as they were.

If the account owner requested immediate deletion when cancelling, Kestrowe CRM erases the account's data within 7 days and the account cannot be restored. After the 90-day window, Kestrowe CRM permanently deletes contacts, deals, notes and attachments, and support cannot restore them.

Exports are available throughout the archived period. Owners can download contacts and deals as CSV files and attachments as a single ZIP archive from Settings > Data > Export.

sources.title: Failed payments and suspended accounts
sources.text:
Kestrowe CRM charges the card on file at the start of each billing period. If a payment fails, the billing system tries the card again 3 days later and once more after another 3 days. The account owner and any billing contacts receive an email after each failed attempt with a link to update the payment method.

If all three attempts fail, the account is suspended. Regular users cannot sign in to a suspended account, but the owner can still reach the Billing page. Paying the outstanding balance lifts the suspension straight away, and no data is lost while an account is suspended.

A suspended account that remains unpaid for 30 days is cancelled automatically. From that point the normal cancellation rules apply, in the same way as if the owner had cancelled the subscription themselves. Kestrowe CRM does not charge late fees or interest on overdue balances.

gold.target_claim: Any cancelled Kestrowe CRM account can be reactivated with all of its data within 90 days of cancellation.

gold_spans.quote: If the account owner did not request immediate deletion, a cancelled Kestrowe CRM account can be reactivated with all of its data within 90 days of cancellation.

gold.dropped_qualifier: If the account owner did not request immediate deletion

construction.note: The no-immediate-deletion condition was deleted; S2 makes reactivation depend on it (accounts with immediate deletion cannot be restored), so the unconditional claim is not supported.

question: How much does extra backup storage cost on Halvanta Backup?
answer: Halvanta Backup workspaces can add backup storage in 500 GB blocks for $12 per block per month.

sources.title: Version history and retention
sources.text:
Halvanta Backup keeps earlier versions of files so that accidental changes can be undone. On the Personal plan, file versions and deleted files are kept for 30 days. On the Team plan they are kept for 1 year, and on the Business plan an admin can set retention to any period between 1 and 7 years.

Retention is counted from the day a version is replaced or a file is deleted on the device, not from the day it was first backed up. Versions that are older than the retention period are removed during a nightly clean-up and no longer count toward storage.

Admins on Team and Business can place a device on hold when an employee leaves. A held device stops backing up, but its existing backups are kept until the hold is released, even if they are older than the retention period. Held devices are not billed as active devices.

sources.title: Halvanta Backup plans
sources.text:
Halvanta Backup has three plans. Personal costs $6 per month and protects one computer, with unlimited backup storage for files on that computer's internal drives. External drives can be added for $2 per drive per month.

The Team plan costs $8 per device per month, with a minimum of 3 devices. Each device includes 1 TB of backup storage, and storage is pooled across the workspace, so a device that uses less leaves room for one that uses more. Team workspaces get an admin console, device groups and email support. Annual billing for Team is also available at a discounted rate.

The Business plan is for organisations protecting 50 or more devices and is priced by quote. It adds single sign-on, legal hold, a dedicated support contact and a choice of data region at sign-up.

Prices exclude sales tax and VAT, which are added at checkout based on the billing address.

sources.title: Buying extra storage on the Team plan
sources.text:
When a Team workspace needs more space than its pooled allowance, an admin can buy storage add-ons instead of adding devices. On the Team plan, Halvanta Backup workspaces can add backup storage in 500 GB blocks for $12 per block per month. Blocks join the workspace's shared pool as soon as the purchase is confirmed and can be used by any device in the workspace.

Each Team plan workspace can hold a maximum of 20 add-on blocks at a time, which adds up to 10 TB of extra storage.

Blocks are bought and removed from Admin console > Billing > Storage. A block can only be removed if the workspace's stored data still fits within the remaining allowance after the removal. Removed blocks stop appearing on invoices from the next billing period. If stored data goes over the total allowance, new backups pause until space is freed or more storage is added; existing backups are not deleted.

gold.target_claim: Halvanta Backup workspaces on any plan can add backup storage in 500 GB blocks for $12 per block per month.

gold_spans.quote: On the Team plan, Halvanta Backup workspaces can add backup storage in 500 GB blocks for $12 per block per month.

construction.note: The Team plan scope was deleted; S3 describes add-on blocks only for Team workspaces and no passage gives them for Personal or Business, so the plan-wide claim is not supported.

question: What discount do Ferncroft Forms Classic subscribers get for moving to Pro?
answer: Classic subscribers can switch to the Pro plan at a 30% discount for the first year.

sources.title: Retiring the Classic plan
sources.text:
Ferncroft Forms stops selling the Classic plan to new customers on 15 January 2027. Workspaces already on Classic are not moved automatically: existing Classic subscriptions keep renewing at their current price, with the same features and limits.

To help Classic subscribers move to the current plan line-up, Ferncroft Forms is offering a discount on the Pro plan. Between 15 January and 15 July 2027, Classic subscribers can switch to the Pro plan at a 30% discount for the first year. The discount applies to the Pro list price for twelve months from the date of the switch and then ends, so from the second year the workspace pays the standard Pro price. The offer ends on 15 July 2027, and switches made after that date are charged the standard Pro price from the start.

A workspace that switches to Pro cannot return to Classic later, because Classic will no longer be open for sign-up. Workspace owners can make the switch from Settings > Plan > Explore plans.

sources.title: Ferncroft Forms Pro plan
sources.text:
The Pro plan is Ferncroft Forms' main plan for teams that collect data at volume. It costs $24 per month on monthly billing or $240 per year on annual billing, and includes 5 team members, unlimited forms and 10,000 responses per month. Additional team members cost $6 per month each.

Pro adds features that are not available on the Starter plan: conditional logic with up to 50 rules per form, file upload fields with 10 GB of total file storage, custom thank-you pages and removal of Ferncroft branding. Payment fields on Pro connect to a card processor of your choice, and Ferncroft Forms charges no additional transaction fee.

The Business plan, at $59 per month, raises the response allowance to 50,000 per month, adds single sign-on and allows data residency in the EU or Australia. Both plans include a 14-day free trial for new workspaces, with no payment card required.

sources.title: What happens when you reach your response limit
sources.text:
Each Ferncroft Forms plan includes a monthly number of form responses, counted across every form in the workspace. The count resets on the first day of each billing period. Partial submissions that are saved but never sent are not counted.

When a workspace reaches 90% of its allowance, owners see a warning banner and receive an email. Once the allowance is used up, live forms show a message saying the form is temporarily closed, and new responses are not accepted until the next billing period starts or the workspace changes plan. Responses already collected stay available to view and export.

Pro and Business workspaces can turn on overage instead of closing forms. With overage on, forms keep accepting responses, and each extra block of 1,000 responses is charged at $8 on the next invoice. Overage can be capped at a monthly spending limit set by the owner.

gold.target_claim: Ferncroft Forms Classic subscribers can switch to the Pro plan at a 30% discount for the first year, at any time.

gold_spans.quote: Between 15 January and 15 July 2027, Classic subscribers can switch to the Pro plan at a 30% discount for the first year.

question: Can Orrin Freight's Veltrano Maps project briefly go above its normal geocoding rate limit?
answer: Orrin Freight's Veltrano Maps project can burst its geocoding traffic to 800 RPS for up to 30 seconds.

sources.title: Veltrano Maps pricing: credits and overage
sources.text:
Veltrano Maps bills API usage in credits. A forward or reverse geocoding request uses 1 credit, a route optimisation request uses 5 credits, and a static map image uses 2 credits. Each plan includes a monthly credit allowance: Sandbox includes 10,000 credits, Builder includes 400,000 credits and Scale includes 6,000,000 credits. Unused credits expire at the end of the billing month and do not roll over.

Usage beyond the allowance is charged as overage at the end of the month. Builder overage costs $0.60 per 1,000 credits and Scale overage costs $0.35 per 1,000 credits. Sandbox projects cannot incur overage; once the allowance is used up, further requests return HTTP 402 until the next billing month begins.

You can set a monthly spending cap from the billing page. When the cap is reached, Veltrano Maps sends an email to every project owner and stops serving billable requests until the cap is raised or the month ends. Changes to the cap take effect within five minutes.

sources.title: Rate limits for the Veltrano Maps REST API
sources.text:
Every request to the Veltrano Maps REST API counts toward a per-project limit measured in requests per second (RPS). The limit depends on the plan the project is billed under:

- Sandbox: 5 RPS for geocoding and 2 RPS for route optimisation.
- Builder: 50 RPS for geocoding and 10 RPS for route optimisation.
- Scale: 400 RPS for geocoding and 60 RPS for route optimisation.

Scale projects may burst to 800 RPS on geocoding for up to 30 seconds, provided the project has a verified billing contact on file. Bursting is not available on Sandbox or Builder projects.

When a project goes over its limit, the API responds with HTTP 429 and a Retry-After header giving the number of seconds to wait before retrying. Requests rejected with HTTP 429 are not billed. Limits are applied per project, not per API key, so creating additional keys within the same project does not raise the ceiling.

If you need a higher sustained limit than your plan provides, contact the solutions team from the project dashboard. Requests for custom limits are reviewed within five business days.

sources.title: Map tiles: connection limits and caching
sources.text:
Map tiles are served from a separate content delivery network and are not counted toward the REST API limits described elsewhere in this documentation. Instead, tile traffic is limited by the number of concurrent connections a project can hold open: 4 on Sandbox, 32 on Builder and 256 on Scale.

Vector tiles are cached at the edge for 24 hours and raster tiles for 7 days. If you restyle a map, add a new style version to the tile URL so that clients fetch fresh tiles instead of waiting for the cache to expire.

Tile requests must include the project's public token, which begins with pk_. Public tokens are safe to embed in browser and mobile code because they can only read tiles and styles; they cannot call geocoding or routing endpoints. You can restrict a public token to a list of allowed referrer domains or mobile bundle identifiers from the token settings page. Requests from a domain that is not on the list receive HTTP 403.

sources.title: Customer story: Orrin Freight
sources.text:
Orrin Freight moved its dispatch platform to Veltrano Maps in early 2025, replacing an in-house geocoder that struggled during the morning rush. The engineering team now sends every address lookup for its 1,400 drivers through a single Veltrano Maps project on the Scale plan.

According to the company's platform lead, the busiest period is between 6 and 8 in the morning, when route sheets are generated for the whole fleet at once. Since the move, the share of delivery addresses matched on the first attempt has risen from 91 percent to 98 percent, and the team no longer maintains its own geocoding servers.

Orrin Freight also uses Veltrano route optimisation to group deliveries by vehicle capacity and delivery window. The company plans to extend the same project to its new cold-chain division later this year, adding about 300 refrigerated vehicles. The project is administered by the platform team, and usage reports are shared with the operations group every week.

gold.target_claim: Orrin Freight's Veltrano Maps project is able to burst geocoding traffic to 800 RPS for up to 30 seconds.

gold_spans.quote: a single Veltrano Maps project on the Scale plan
Scale projects may burst to 800 RPS on geocoding for up to 30 seconds, provided the project has a verified billing contact on file.

construction.note: S4 puts Orrin on Scale and S2 lets Scale projects burst, but only with a verified billing contact; the bridge that Orrin's project has one is stated nowhere, so the passages do not jointly entail the claim.

question: Will my app on the Kestrelline Node.js SDK 6.x break when version 2025-02 is retired?
answer: Requests sent with the Kestrelline Node.js SDK 6.x will be rejected with HTTP 410 once version 2025-02 is retired.

sources.title: Changelog: Kestrelline Messaging API version 2026-02
sources.text:
Version 2026-02 is the current version of the Kestrelline Messaging API. It was released on 1 February 2026 and includes the following changes compared with version 2025-02.

- The status field on message objects now uses queued, sent, delivered, failed and expired. The former value undeliverable is reported as failed with a failure_code.
- Phone numbers in every request and response are formatted in E.164. Local formats are no longer accepted.
- The /messages endpoint returns 202 Accepted instead of 200 OK, because delivery happens asynchronously.
- Media attachments are limited to 5 MB per message, up from 2 MB.
- The /send endpoint has been removed; use /messages instead.

To upgrade, change the Kestrelline-Version header in one service at a time and watch for failed requests in the request log. The request log shows the version each request was served with, which makes it easy to find a service that still sends the old value.

sources.title: Kestrelline Messaging API: version lifecycle
sources.text:
The Kestrelline Messaging API is versioned by release date. You choose a version by sending the Kestrelline-Version header, for example Kestrelline-Version: 2026-02. Requests without the header use the version that was pinned to your account when it was created.

Each version moves through three stages. A version is current until a newer one is released. It is then deprecated for 12 months, during which it keeps working without changes. After that it is retired, and requests that name it are rejected with HTTP 410 Gone.

Version 2025-02 was deprecated on 1 February 2026 and will be retired on 1 February 2027. From 1 November 2026 to 31 January 2027, responses to requests that specify version 2025-02 include a Sunset header carrying the retirement date. We will also run two one-hour brownouts, on 12 January 2027 and 26 January 2027, during which those requests fail with HTTP 410 so that you can confirm nothing still depends on the old version.

Webhook payloads are rendered with the version pinned to the endpoint when it was created, not the version of the request that triggered the event. Upgrade your webhook endpoints separately from the API calls your application makes.

sources.title: Kestrelline Node.js SDK 6.x release notes
sources.text:
Version 6.0.0 of the Kestrelline Node.js SDK was released on 14 March 2025 and was built and tested against API version 2025-02. Its type definitions describe the message, contact and webhook objects exactly as that version returns them. The SDK sends a Kestrelline-Version header only when you set the apiVersion option on the client.

Other changes in 6.x:
- Message objects are returned as typed classes instead of plain objects.
- Automatic retries apply only to requests that fail with HTTP 429 or a network error, and are capped at three attempts.
- Support for Node.js 16 has been removed; the minimum is Node.js 18.
- A new paginate helper iterates through list endpoints without manual cursor handling.

Version 6.4.2, released in August 2026, is the last planned 6.x release. Version 7.0.0 was built against API version 2026-02 and adds typed classes for the new message statuses. Release notes for each version are published on the day it ships.

gold.target_claim: All requests made through the Kestrelline Node.js SDK 6.x will fail with HTTP 410 after version 2025-02 is retired.

gold_spans.quote: was built and tested against API version 2025-02
The SDK sends a Kestrelline-Version header only when you set the apiVersion option on the client.
Requests without the header use the version that was pinned to your account when it was created.
After that it is retired, and requests that name it are rejected with HTTP 410 Gone.

construction.note: 'Built against 2025-02' (S3) plus 'retired versions return 410' (S2) tempts the claim, but by default the SDK sends no version header, so requests use the account's pinned version; the bridge that the account (and every client) is on 2025-02 is stated nowhere.

question: Should my small shop turn on extended retries for Ondrel Billing webhooks?
answer: Turning on extended retries is the best way for a small merchant to make sure no payment events are ever missed.

sources.title: Ondrel Billing webhook event types
sources.text:
Subscribe each webhook endpoint only to the events your integration handles. You can change an endpoint's subscriptions at any time; the change applies to events created after you save it.

Invoices
- invoice.created - a draft invoice was generated for a subscription or a one-off charge.
- invoice.finalized - the invoice was locked and sent to the customer.
- invoice.paid - payment succeeded in full.
- invoice.payment_failed - a payment attempt was declined or returned an error.

Subscriptions
- subscription.created, subscription.updated and subscription.cancelled.
- subscription.trial_ending - sent 3 days before a trial converts to a paid plan.

Customers
- customer.created and customer.updated.
- customer.tax_id_verified - a tax identifier passed validation.

Each event payload contains an id, a type, a created_at timestamp and a data object holding the full resource as it was when the event occurred. Events are kept in the event log for 30 days, where you can inspect payloads and see the response your endpoint returned to every attempt.

sources.title: Ondrel Billing webhooks: delivery and retries
sources.text:
Ondrel Billing sends each webhook event to your endpoint as an HTTPS POST request with a JSON body. Respond with any 2xx status within 10 seconds to acknowledge the event; slower responses are recorded as timeouts and count as failed deliveries.

Extended retries. From 1 December 2026, Ondrel Billing retries a failed webhook delivery for up to 72 hours if the endpoint has extended retries enabled. Retries use exponential backoff, starting at 1 minute and capped at 6 hours between attempts. Turn on extended retries for each endpoint under Settings > Developers > Webhooks.

Duplicates and ordering. Every attempt for the same event carries the same value in the Ondrel-Event-Id header, so your handler can discard events it has already processed. Events are not guaranteed to arrive in the order they were created; compare the created_at field in the payload if ordering matters.

Disabled endpoints. If every delivery to an endpoint has failed for 5 consecutive days, the endpoint is disabled automatically and the account owner is notified by email. Fix the underlying problem, then re-enable the endpoint from the same settings page. Events that occurred while the endpoint was disabled are not redelivered automatically, but you can replay them from the event log.

sources.title: Receiving test webhooks with the Ondrel command-line tool
sources.text:
The Ondrel command-line tool lets you receive test-mode webhook events on your own machine without exposing a public URL. After signing in with ondrel login, run ondrel listen --forward-to localhost:4000/hooks and the tool relays every test-mode event from your account to that local address.

The terminal shows each event type as it arrives, along with the status code your local server returned. To generate an event on demand, run ondrel trigger followed by an event type, for example ondrel trigger invoice.paid. Triggered events use fixture data and do not create real customers or charges.

Events relayed this way carry livemode set to false, so you can guard against processing them in production code. The listen command relays only events created while it is running; it does not fetch older events from the event log. A listen session ends after 8 hours, after which you need to run the command again. Live-mode events are never relayed by the command-line tool.

gold.target_claim: Enabling extended retries is the best way for a small merchant to guarantee no payment events are missed.

construction.note: Judgement ('best way', 'ever missed') that the delivery docs cannot settle.

question: If I create a guest code while I'm at work, will it work on my Keyway lock straight away?
answer: New guest codes work immediately on Keyway locks.

sources.title: Charging the Keyway Pro battery pack
sources.text:
The Keyway Pro is powered by a rechargeable battery pack that slides out of the inside part of the lock. A full charge usually lasts between four and six months, depending on how often the door is locked and unlocked and how many people in your home use Auto-Unlock.

When the pack drops to 15 percent, the Pellora app sends a low-battery alert and the keypad light flashes amber after each use. At 5 percent, the lock stops using Auto-Unlock to save power, but you can still lock and unlock it with the app, the keypad or the key.

To charge it, press the release tab, slide the pack out, and connect it to a USB-C charger. Charging from empty takes about three hours, and the light on the pack turns solid green when it is full. While the pack is out, the lock cannot be operated electronically, so keep your physical key handy or charge the pack while you are at home.

A spare pack lets you swap without waiting. Spare packs are sold separately in the Pellora app under Shop.

sources.title: Creating guest codes for your Keyway lock
sources.text:
Guest codes let visitors, cleaners or dog walkers open your door with the keypad, without needing the Pellora app. To create one, open the app, choose your lock, and tap Access > Guest codes > New code.

New guest codes work immediately, but only on locks that are within range of a Pellora Bridge. A lock without a bridge receives new codes the next time a phone with the Pellora app comes within Bluetooth range of it.

You can make a code permanent, limit it to certain days and times, or set it to expire after a single use. Each Keyway lock holds up to 30 guest codes at a time.

When someone uses a guest code, the lock's owner gets a notification showing the code's name, so give each code a name you will recognise. Deleting a code follows the same rule as creating one: it takes effect straight away on locks with a bridge, and otherwise the next time a phone with the app is nearby.

gold.target_claim: New guest codes work immediately on every Keyway lock.

gold_spans.quote: New guest codes work immediately, but only on locks that are within range of a Pellora Bridge.

gold.dropped_qualifier: but only on locks that are within range of a Pellora Bridge

question: Will my Arc Plus warn me when the air in my home gets too dry?
answer: Arc Plus thermostats can send Dry Air alerts.

sources.title: Dry Air alerts
sources.text:
Dry Air alerts let you know when the air in your home is getting too dry, which often happens in winter when the heating runs for long periods. When indoor humidity stays below 30 percent for more than two hours, you get a notification in the Tessaline Home app with tips for raising it.

Dry Air alerts are available on Tessaline thermostats that have a built-in humidity sensor and are running software version 5.5 or later. To check your version, open the Tessaline Home app and go to Settings > About.

To turn the alerts on or off, go to Settings > Notifications > Dry Air. Only the person who set up the thermostat can change this setting, but once the alerts are on, everyone in the home receives them.

Dry Air alerts do not control humidifiers. If you have a whole-home humidifier, manage it with its own controls.

sources.title: Filter change reminders
sources.text:
Arc can remind you when it is time to change the air filter in your heating and cooling system. Reminders are based on how many hours your system has actually run, not on calendar days, so a mild season stretches the time between reminders.

By default, Arc reminds you after 500 hours of fan run time. If your filter's packaging recommends a different interval, change it under Settings > Equipment > Filter reminder. You can choose any value from 100 to 1,500 hours in steps of 50.

When a reminder is due, a banner appears in the Tessaline Home app and a small filter icon appears on the thermostat's display. After you replace the filter, tap Reset on the banner, or press and hold the filter icon on Arc for three seconds, to start counting again.

If you have more than one Arc in your home, each thermostat keeps its own count. Turning filter reminders off does not change your schedule or any other setting.

sources.title: Arc Plus at a glance
sources.text:
Arc Plus is the larger of our two thermostats. It has a 3.5-inch colour display, a built-in humidity sensor, and a presence sensor that wakes the display when you walk up to it. Like the standard Arc, it works with most gas, oil and electric heating systems, as well as central air conditioning and heat pumps.

Arc Plus comes with one Tessaline Room Sensor in the box. Place it in the room where you spend the most time, and Arc Plus can balance the temperature between that room and the hallway where the thermostat is mounted. You can add up to five more room sensors.

Arc Plus needs a common wire, often called a C-wire, for power. If your system does not have one, the Power Adapter Kit, sold separately in the Tessaline Home app, provides it.

Arc Plus comes in white, charcoal and brushed steel finishes.

gold.target_claim: Arc Plus thermostats can send Dry Air alerts.

gold_spans.quote: It has a 3.5-inch colour display, a built-in humidity sensor, and a presence sensor that wakes the display when you walk up to it.
Dry Air alerts are available on Tessaline thermostats that have a built-in humidity sensor and are running software version 5.5 or later.

construction.note: S3 gives Arc Plus a humidity sensor and S1 makes Dry Air alerts depend on that sensor plus software 5.5 or later; no passage says which software Arc Plus runs, so the claim needs the unstated bridge that it is on 5.5 or later.

question: Will two-step verification keep my doorbell footage safe?
answer: Requiring two-step verification will stop anyone from gaining unauthorised access to your Vista Doorbell footage.

sources.title: Adding and removing shared users
sources.text:
You can share your Vista Doorbell with the people you live with so they can see who is at the door. Go to Account > Household, tap Invite, and enter the person's email address. They receive an invitation that stays valid for 7 days; if it expires, send a new one from the same screen.

Each account can have up to 8 shared users. Shared users can watch live video, view recorded clips, talk through the doorbell, and receive motion and ring alerts. They cannot change device settings, delete clips, manage your subscription, or invite other people.

To remove someone, open Account > Household, tap their name, and choose Remove. They lose access straight away. Any clips they downloaded to their own phone before you removed them stay on their phone.

If a shared user says they cannot see your doorbell, ask them to check that they accepted the invitation using the same email address you entered. Invitations cannot be moved from one email address to another.

sources.title: Resetting your Corvane password
sources.text:
If you have forgotten your password, tap Forgot password on the sign-in screen of the Corvane app and enter the email address on your account. We send you a reset link that works once and expires after 60 minutes.

Your new password must be at least 10 characters long and cannot match any of your last five passwords. After you change it, every phone and browser signed in to your account is signed out, including the Corvane app on your own phone, so you will need to sign in again.

Changing your password does not affect your shared users. They keep their access and continue to sign in with their own details.

If the reset email does not arrive within a few minutes, check your spam or junk folder, and make sure you entered the address you used when you created the account. For security reasons, Corvane support cannot set a password for you or tell you your password over the phone.

sources.title: Two-step verification for your Corvane account
sources.text:
Two-step verification adds a second check when someone signs in to your Corvane account. After entering your password, you confirm the sign-in with a six-digit code, either sent to you by text message or generated in an authenticator app.

Starting 2 March 2026, the Corvane app requires two-step verification for account owners who have invited shared users. Shared users are people you have added under Account > Household so that they can watch live video from your Vista Doorbell and receive its alerts. If this applies to you and you have not set up two-step verification by that date, the app asks you to set it up the next time you sign in, and live video stays locked until you finish.

To set it up at any time, go to Account > Security > Two-step verification and follow the prompts.

When you finish setup, the app shows ten single-use backup codes. Keep them somewhere safe and away from your phone: if you lose access to your phone, a backup code lets you sign in once. You can generate a new set at any time from the same screen, and doing so cancels any codes you have not used.

Shared users sign in with their own Corvane accounts. Their security settings are separate from yours, and turning on two-step verification for your account does not change how they sign in.

gold.target_claim: Requiring two-step verification will prevent all unauthorised access to Vista Doorbell footage.

construction.note: A prediction about security outcomes; the passages describe how two-step verification works but cannot settle whether it will stop all unauthorised access.

question: Is Ondrel deleting my old alarm history?
answer: All alarm events will be permanently deleted on 1 December 2026.

sources.title: How long camera clips are kept
sources.text:
Clips from Wardline cameras are saved to the cloud when motion is detected or an alarm goes off. How long they are kept depends on your plan.

Wardline Essentials keeps clips for 7 days. Wardline Plus keeps clips for 30 days, and Wardline Pro Monitoring keeps them for 60 days. Clips recorded during an alarm are kept for 90 days on every plan, so that you have time to share them with your insurer or the police.

When you change plan, the new retention period applies to clips recorded after the change. Clips you already have keep the retention period they were saved with.

To keep a clip for longer, open it in the History tab and tap Download. Downloaded clips are saved to your phone and are not deleted when the cloud copy expires. Deleting a clip in the app removes the cloud copy only; anything you have downloaded stays on your device.

sources.title: Changes to alarm history in the Ondrel app
sources.text:
We are moving alarm history to a new storage system so that the History tab loads faster and can be searched.

All alarm events recorded between 1 January 2023 and 31 May 2024 will be permanently deleted on 1 December 2026. Once they are deleted, Ondrel support cannot recover them.

If you want to keep a copy of these events, download them before the deletion date. In the app, go to Settings > Account > Download my data and choose Alarm history. The file arrives by email as a CSV within 24 hours. Each download covers up to 12 months of events, so you may need to request more than one.

This change affects alarm events only: arming and disarming, sensor triggers, panic button presses and siren activations. Camera clips are stored separately and follow the retention period of your plan.

Only the account owner can request a download. Shared users can still view alarm history in the app but cannot export it.

sources.title: Arming your system on a schedule
sources.text:
An arming schedule sets your Wardline system to Home or Away automatically at the times you choose, so you do not have to remember to arm it every night.

To create one, go to Settings > Security > Arming schedule and tap Add. Choose the mode, the time and the days of the week. You can add up to 6 schedules per system. Schedules follow the time zone set for your home, not the time zone of your phone.

Five minutes before a scheduled arming, everyone on the account who has notifications turned on receives a reminder. If a door or window is open at that time, the system arms anyway and leaves that sensor out until it is closed, and the app tells you which sensor was skipped.

Schedules can only arm the system. Disarming always needs a code, the app or a key fob, so a schedule will never disarm Wardline for you.

question: How much paid parental leave do primary caregivers get at Brennholt Logistics?
answer: Primary caregivers receive 18 weeks of parental leave at full base pay.

sources.title: Brennholt Logistics Employee Handbook - 6.1 Annual Leave
sources.text:
All permanent employees at Brennholt Logistics receive 25 days of paid annual leave per leave year, plus the eight public holidays observed in England and Wales. The leave year runs from 1 January to 31 December. Employees who join or leave part-way through the year receive a pro-rata entitlement, rounded up to the nearest half day.

Part-time employees receive annual leave in proportion to their contracted hours. For example, an employee contracted for three days a week receives 15 days of annual leave plus a pro-rata share of public holidays.

After five years of continuous service, the entitlement rises to 27 days. After ten years it rises to 29 days. The increase applies from the start of the leave year following the service anniversary.

Leave requests should be submitted through the HR portal at least two weeks in advance for absences of three days or more. Managers may decline a request during the November and December peak period if minimum staffing levels in a depot would not be met.

Up to five days of unused annual leave can be carried into the first three months of the following leave year. Carried-over days that are not taken by 31 March are lost, unless the employee could not take them because of sickness or family leave.

sources.title: Brennholt Logistics Employee Handbook - 6.2 Parental Leave
sources.text:
Brennholt Logistics supports employees who are welcoming a child through birth, adoption or surrogacy. This section sets out company parental pay for permanent employees of any gender.

Primary caregivers who have completed 26 weeks of continuous service by the expected date of birth or placement receive 18 weeks of parental leave at full base pay. Secondary caregivers who meet the same service condition receive 6 weeks of parental leave at full base pay. Employees who have not reached 26 weeks of service are still entitled to unpaid parental leave and to any statutory payments, but not to the enhanced company pay described in this section.

Paid parental leave may be taken in one continuous block or in up to three separate blocks of at least two weeks each. All paid parental leave must be taken within 52 weeks of the birth or placement, and any weeks not used by then are lost.

Employees should tell their line manager and the People team about their plans at least eight weeks before the intended start date, using the parental leave form in the HR portal.

Where both parents work for Brennholt, one parent is designated the primary caregiver and the other the secondary caregiver. The two entitlements cannot be combined so that one parent takes both.

During paid parental leave, pension contributions, life assurance and private medical cover continue as if the employee were at work, and annual leave continues to accrue.

sources.title: Brennholt Logistics Employee Handbook - 6.3 Time Off for Appointments
sources.text:
Employees who are pregnant are entitled to paid time off to attend antenatal appointments advised by a midwife, doctor or registered nurse, including parenting classes where these have been recommended. Brennholt does not limit the number of antenatal appointments, but asks employees to book them at the start or end of a shift where this is practical.

The partner of a pregnant employee, or an intended parent in a surrogacy arrangement, may take paid time off to attend up to two antenatal appointments of up to six and a half hours each.

Employees who are adopting may take paid time off to attend up to five adoption meetings before the child is placed with them. Where two people are adopting jointly, the second adopter may attend up to two of these meetings with pay.

Employees undergoing fertility treatment may take up to five days of paid leave in any rolling 12-month period for appointments and procedures. Their partner may take up to two days of paid leave in the same period to attend appointments with them.

Please record every appointment in the HR portal under 'Medical and family appointments' so that the time is paid correctly. Managers may ask to see an appointment card or letter for any appointment after the first.
